Do the following using the steps provided in their respective sections.
        Steps:
        1. clone the repo git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
        2. analyse the contents of the repo and create following.
            2.1 create/update dockerfile based on the analysis. 
            2.2 kubernetes yamls based on the analysis.
            2.3 github actions file to build application on pushing to main branch.
        3. add all changed file to git changes 
        4. commit / push to repo

function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run inside a script) to finish the whole pipeline.  
I’ll also paste the exact file contents that you should end up with – just replace the placeholders (`<YOUR‑REGISTRY>`, `<YOUR‑USERNAME>` etc.) with your own values.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> If you don’t have SSH keys set up, you can clone via HTTPS instead:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & generate artefacts

### 2.1 What the repo looks like (quick snapshot)

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `package.json` | Node dependencies + start script |
| `app.js` (or `src/index.js`) | Main entry point – usually an Express server |
| `.gitignore` | Standard Node ignore list |

> **Assumption**: The app listens on `process.env.PORT || 3000`.  
> If it’s different, adjust the Dockerfile/K8s port accordingly.

### 2.2 Create / update the Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` at the repo root with the following content:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Install dependencies first (cached layer)
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> *Why this Dockerfile?*  
> - Uses the official lightweight `node:18-alpine` image.  
> - Caches `npm ci` so subsequent builds only rebuild when `package-lock.json` changes.  
> - Exposes port **3000** (adjust if your app uses another port).

### 2.3 Generate Kubernetes YAMLs

Create a directory called `k8s` (if it doesn’t exist):

```bash
mkdir -p k8s
```

Inside `k8s`, create two files:

#### `k8s/deployment.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR-REGISTRY>/<YOUR-USERNAME>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
```

#### `k8s/service.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer          # Change to NodePort/ClusterIP if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80                  # External port
    targetPort: 3000          # Container port
```

> **Tip**: If you’re running on a cluster without external LB support (e.g., Minikube), change `type: LoadBalancer` to `NodePort`.

### 2.4 Create a GitHub Actions workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows` if it doesn’t exist:

```bash
mkdir -p .github/workflows
```

Create a file `.github/workflows/build-and-push.yml` with:

```yaml
name: CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build_and_push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        push: true
        tags: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **What you need to set up**  
> 1. In your GitHub repo → Settings → Secrets → Actions → New repository secret  
>    - `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME`: Your Docker Hub username  
>    - `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`: A Docker Hub personal access token (with “write” scope)  

> **If you want to push to GitHub Container Registry instead** replace the login step with:

```yaml
    - name: Log in to GHCR
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

and change the `tags:` line to `ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest`.

---

## 3️⃣ Stage the new files

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/build-and-push.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> After pushing, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically trigger on the next push to `main`.  
> You should see the job “CI/CD” run in the Actions tab of your repo.

---

### Quick sanity check

Once the workflow finishes successfully, you can test the image locally:

```bash
docker pull <YOUR-REGISTRY>/<YOUR-USERNAME>/nodejs-welcome:latest
docker run -d -p 8080:3000 <YOUR-REGISTRY>/<YOUR-USERNAME>/nodejs-welcome:latest
curl http://localhost:8080
```

You should get the same response as when you run `node app.js` locally.

---

That’s it! 🎉  
Feel free to tweak the replica count, environment variables, or service type to fit your production needs.
